subject: FastCart discovery — TTFT targets and streaming cadence proposal
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@fastcart.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 15:24:00 -0700
Subject: FastCart discovery — TTFT targets and streaming cadence proposal

Hi Daniel — thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and a proposed next step so we can align on performance commitments before the pilot: 

Summary from call:
- Primary objective: reduce perceived latency for end users during cart checkout flows (token-limited prompts, ~120–300 tokens).
- Constraint: bursty traffic from campaigns with short peaks (anticipated concurrency up to ~300 concurrent streams).
- Security/compliance: current FastCart instance in us-west-2, inbound connections allowed from standard Redwood endpoints.

Proposal (what we want to validate in a short probe):
1) TTFT target: aim for <= 200ms P95 on typical payloads (50–150 token outputs) and <= 120ms median.
2) Streaming: prefer SSE for simple browser clients; WebSocket for mobile SDKs if we detect unstable client reconnects.
3) Chunk cadence: initial chunk within TTFT above, then subsequent chunks every 80–120ms (configurable) to keep UI responsive without excess small packets.
4) Throughput/concurrency: validate sustained 300 concurrent streams for 5 minutes with <10% tail degradation.

Next steps I propose:
- We run a 48-hour probe (low-effort) to collect TTFT distribution and packet cadence data. I attached a short probe plan that outlines sample payloads and ramp steps.
- Internal engineering sync to decide default chunk size and fallback to polling for mobile edge cases.

Attachments: fastcart-ttft-probe-plan.md (probe steps + payloads)

Can you confirm those targets or flag anything that would block the pilot? If that works, I’ll schedule the probe early next week and loop Rishi/Kimberly for ops/infra sign-off.

Best,
Avery
Avery Johnson
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.com
(Attachment: fastcart-ttft-probe-plan.md)

From: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@fastcart.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FastCart discovery — TTFT targets and streaming cadence proposal

Thanks Avery — that matches what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications from the Ops side: 

- TTFT floor: our UX lead wants any P95 >= 250ms to be escalated; ideally we keep P95 below 200ms but we can accept up to 250ms during peak if we have a clear mitigation.
- Concurrency: 300 concurrent is correct for expected holiday peaks; we also see very short spikes up to ~500 for 30–60s during flash deals.
- Streaming preference: we prefer SSE for web because of simpler reconnection semantics, but mobile team will want WebSocket fallback for partial payload resumption.
- Chunking: smaller initial chunk is helpful (first 1–2 tokens quickly) but we care most about perceived first output — anything that improves render time at the 0–250ms window is valuable.

We’re good with a 48-hour probe. Two asks:
1) Include a CSV with sample expected request/response sizes so our infra team can pre-provision capacity (ttft_probe_summary.csv would be perfect).
2) Can you confirm whether Redwood can do automatic fallback to a lower-capacity model variant under load (with a defined SLO for detection/fallback)? That will determine whether we require a hard SLO or a degradation-with-fallback plan.

If you can share the probe plan and sample CSV today we’ll review and greenlight.

—Daniel
Daniel Ruiz
Head of Platform Engineering, FastCart
daniel.ruiz@fastcart.com
(External: FastCart Ops <ops@fastcart.com>)

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@fastcart.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: FastCart discovery — TTFT targets and streaming cadence proposal

Rishi/Kim — forwarding Daniel’s confirmation. Two things we need from infra/runtime:

1) Fallback behavior: Daniel asked whether Redwood can automatically route to a lower-cost/quantized model when we detect token-supply/backpressure or GPU contention. Ideally this is seamless and takes <500ms to switch kernels/instances with KV cache compatibility. If we can’t do automatic hot-swap, we should propose an explicit failover policy.

2) Chunk cadence experiments: propose we try two cadences in the probe (A/B):
   - Cadence A: initial chunk at first-token, follow-ups every 120ms (coarser).
   - Cadence B: initial chunk plus a short priming packet at ~60ms then regular 80ms cadence (more aggressive).

Probe instrumentation notes: collect TTFT per-device-type (desktop vs mobile), P50/P95/P99, token throughput, and chunk sizes. I attached a short CSV template and the probe plan.

Attachment: ttft_probe_summary.csv (payload examples + expected sizes)
Attachment: fastcart-ttft-probe-plan.md

Can you confirm feasibility and add estimated runbook steps we will hand to FastCart Ops?

—Avery
(Attachment references: ttft_probe_summary.csv, fastcart-ttft-probe-plan.md)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@fastcart.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2026 08:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FastCart discovery — TTFT targets and streaming cadence proposal

Avery — quick ops response and recommended next steps (short and actionable):

Feasibility notes:
- TTFT target: we can aim for <= 200ms P95 on the lighter payload mix (50–150 tokens) in us-west-2 using a dedicated pool with continuous batching and prefix caching. P95 <= 250ms is achievable during 500-concurrency short spikes if we pre-warm an additional hot pool (will cost carryover).
- Fallback: we support automatic fallback to a quantized variant (same architecture, 4-bit) with KV cache compatibility. The detection window is ~250–500ms; swap-over is <750ms including cache rewarm in optimistic cases. We can implement an explicit degradation policy for the pilot (preferred) and enable automatic in production once we verify behavior.
- Chunk cadence: both cadence A and B are implementable. My recommendation for the probe: run A for 12 hours, B for 12 hours, then compare TTFT P95 and perceived render (we’ll capture first-byte and first-chunk timing).

Actionable next steps (who/what/when):
- Today: send the final probe plan + CSV to FastCart (Avery) — DONE.
- Tomorrow: pre-provision a 20% over-provision hot pool for the initial probe window. (Owner: Rishi)
- 48-hr probe: start Monday 2026-09-13 09:00 PT. Run A for first 12 hours, B for second 12 hours, then idle and re-run on spike window. (Owner: Avery + FastCart Ops)
- Post-probe: 24-hour analysis + one joint readout call (Owner: Avery + Daniel; invite: Kimberly for infra notes).

I’ll add detailed runbook steps to the drive link and drop a short checklist for FastCart Ops (scheduling, IP allowlist, sample request tokens).

Rishi
